summary:
Australia is entering a new era of integrated urban planning, highlighted by the settlement of the Sydney Plan. This 20-year framework represents a significant shift in how the nation approaches growth, aligning housing, employment, and infrastructure to support a population expanding from 5.3 million to 6.6 million. By treating these elements as a cohesive system rather than isolated projects, the government aims to enhance liveability and ensure that city growth is sustainable and inclusive for all residents.

On the national infrastructure front, the 2026 Priority List emphasizes a multi-modal approach to transport, prioritizing investments in rail, light rail, and zero-emissions bus fleets. These initiatives are designed not only to improve productivity but also to meet net-zero emissions commitments and provide secure, climate-resilient water capacity. Specific attention is being given to high-capacity transport for growing cities, including the Perth rail lines capacity upgrade, which seeks to alleviate pressure on existing networks and improve connectivity for commuters.

Internationally, the focus on transport innovation continues to drive global progress. The World Bank’s Global Facility to Decarbonize Transport (GFDT) is accelerating investment in climate-smart mobility solutions in low and middle-income countries, fostering a global network of sustainable transport. Meanwhile, the broader transport-tech sector is revolutionizing how people and goods move through the world, driven by entrepreneurial innovation and a commitment to sustainable modes of travel, from electric vehicles to biofuel-powered aviation.
